body.heading: Evenings have a shape too
paragraphs: Days have natural beginnings, but evenings often blur: messages, feeds and episodes roll on until sleep interrupts them. Many people find their minds still buzzing from the day's inputs when they get into bed.
A digital sunset gives the evening a hinge. After a chosen time, the bright, busy inputs wind down and slower ones take over: music, paper books, conversation, a walk.

body.heading: Make it easy to keep
paragraphs: Pick a realistic time, perhaps an hour before bed, and set your devices to help: night modes, notification pauses, chargers outside the bedroom if that suits your household.
Expect the first evenings to feel strangely empty, and plan for it. Keep an appealing alternative within reach, and remember you are not banning anything; you are just letting the day end on purpose.

takeaway: Choose a time for screens to quieten, and let the evening soften.
